Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
23-year-old female with 3-day history of constant, worsening midline lower-abdominal pain (8/10) with light post-menstrual vaginal bleeding, nausea (no vomiting), and prior constipation (now resolved). No fever, urinary, or bowel red-flag symptoms. Using etonogestrel implant; last pregnancy test 1 month ago.  
Likely pelvic pathology; ectopic pregnancy must be excluded urgently. Other considerations include pelvic inflammatory disease, ovarian torsion/hemorrhagic cyst. Appendicitis and functional bowel pain less likely but noted.  
Plan agreed:  
• Repeat home pregnancy test today; if positive or symptoms worsen or unable to keep fluids down → immediate medical review.  
• Arrange face-to-face clinic appointment for abdominal and pelvic examination. Caregiver instructed to call support line to schedule.  
• Safety-net advice provided (seek urgent care for escalating pain, syncope, fever, heavy bleeding).

Management Plan
-  Arrange same-day urine pregnancy test; report result.  
-  Book in-person abdominal/pelvic examination via support line.  
-  Escalate to emergency services if positive pregnancy test, increasing pain, vomiting, syncope, or heavy bleeding.  
-  No medications prescribed during tele-visit.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Ectopic pregnancy – High likelihood: reproductive-age woman, lower-abdominal pain, light bleeding, contraception failure possible; pregnancy test >1 month ago.  
2. Pelvic inflammatory disease – Moderate likelihood: lower-abdominal pain, light bleeding/discharge, sexually active; absence of fever and cervical findings lowers probability.  
3. Ovarian torsion or hemorrhagic ovarian cyst – Moderate likelihood: acute constant pelvic pain with possible light bleeding; pain not clearly unilateral but cannot be ruled out.
